main_paper.text: Multi-Representation Underwater Acoustic Object Detection with Generative AI Reasoning Agents
Anonymous authors

Abstract - Underwater acoustic object detection depends on how the same waveform is represented. We compare Fourier spectra, multi-resolution STFT features and Morlet wavelets, individually and in fusion, alongside a two-dimensional log-mel spectrogram CNN. A bounded generative AI controller receives numerical detector evidence from acquired views and may request class-free background replacement. A same-support nuisance edit controls waveform disturbance. A deliberately balanced PORTIA cohort measures three-second AIS-linked window presence, not natural acoustic-event boundaries. Separate temporal-CNN studies evaluate constructed activity unions rather than agent benefit. For Generative agent minus the development-selected Wavelet, AP of mean-seed per-record probabilities differs by -0.017. The five test collection days form one connected day-vessel component; independent-component uncertainty is not estimable. No superiority significance or equivalence claim follows. The study measures component ablations, corruptions and actual end-to-end compute. A bounded HHT approximation remains exploratory after noisy-scene convergence failures. Generated interval replacement is treated as a sensitivity intervention, not physical source removal or causal identification.
Keywords: underwater acoustics; object detection; generative AI; reasoning agents; signal representations; spectrograms; wavelets; Hilbert-Huang transform
1 Introduction

Fourier spectra, spectrograms and wavelets expose different frequency and time structure in the same underwater waveform. We compare their individual and fused detection performance and test bounded tool selection across these representations, with generative verification as an additional probe (Fig. 1). The controller receives numerical head outputs, not images; a separate CNN processes two-dimensional log-mel spectrograms. Detection here means AIS-linked window presence.

main_paper.caption: Fig. 1. Implemented evidence and verification workflow. Fourier, STFT and wavelet measurements are primary. HHT is exploratory. The language model selects tools; the numeric head retains responsibility for calibrated predictions.
main_paper.name: figure1_method

main_paper.text: 2 Related Work and Method

Physics-aware audio-language frameworks already combine complementary acoustic representations with generated reports [2,3]. Underwater audio-language benchmarks test waveform dependence [4], and generative augmentation addresses data scarcity [5]. Wavelet front ends [9] and the HHT decomposition [6] are established methods. Speech-to-ocean transfer [11] motivates a pretrained baseline. The candidate contribution is the paired intervention and tool-selection protocol.
2.1 Acoustic representations and detection

Native audio is preserved; channel 0 is CUDA-resampled to 16 kHz. Fourier, multi-resolution STFT and analytic Morlet views provide 32, 64 and 56 features. Scaling uses training data only. The 32-feature bounded linear-envelope HHT approximation is exploratory after its numerical failure.

main_paper.name: equation_stft
main_paper.text: $S(m,k)=\left|\sum_n x[n]w[n-mH]e^{-j2\pi kn/N}\right|^2$

main_paper.name: equation_hht
main_paper.text: $x(t)=\sum_q c_q(t)+r(t),\quad f_q(t)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\frac{d\phi_q(t)}{dt}$

The primary verification replaces the fixed central 1.5 seconds [0.75, 2.25] of each three-second clip while preserving exterior context. Scoring remains window presence, not source deletion or localization. Baselines include feature heads, a 2D log-mel spectrogram CNN, and frozen speech-ASR pretrained/fine-tuned facebook/wav2vec2-base-960h [12], mean/SD pooled into 1,536 features.
2.2 Generative replacement and paired control

A conditional waveform flow [7] learns background completion. For editable mask M, background b, observation u and Gaussian z, training uses y(t)=M[(1-t)z+tb]+(1-M)u. A same-support sham approximately matches perturbation energy and coarse spectrum: after masking, RMS mismatch must be below 0.05 and eight-band normalized-power L1 error below 0.2. Other engineering gates check finite features, exterior invariance and amplitude. Rejection returns the base score. The full-record null is context-unconditional except for observed-RMS scaling, not a physical counterfactual.

main_paper.name: equation_score
main_paper.text: $V=\mathrm{median}_{v,k}(\delta_{vk})-\lambda\,\mathrm{MAD}_{v,k}(\delta_{vk})-\gamma R$

L is a view-head logit clipped to [-8, 8]. We use K=4 draws, 8 Euler steps, lambda=0.5 and gamma=0.1; medians use the lower central order statistic. R measures exterior change and boundary perturbation. Nonnegative logistic calibration combines base evidence with V. Views are correlated; this acoustic formulation combines familiar robust aggregation and calibration, whose utility must be established empirically.
3 Data and Experimental Protocol

The real study uses a custom PORTIA v2 cohort [1], not the official benchmark split. Its labels reflect AIS-linked vessel co-occurrence, not human judgments of audibility. Single-vessel-task positives and binary-task negatives are combined after excluding 2,388 window IDs with conflicting cross-task labels. Days are allocated before learning; vessel IDs that cross allocated partitions are reserved by test/calibration/development/train priority. A 60-second temporal guard separates partitions. The test cohort is deliberately 600 positive and 600 background clips, not deployment prevalence: AP/precision and probability calibration are cohort-specific.
Table 1. Custom cohort: AIS single-vessel positives and binary-task backgrounds.

Repeated vessel identities connect all five test days into one dependence component. Neither 1,200 clips nor five days are independent deployment replicates. AIS co-occurrence supplies no human audibility judgment or natural acoustic-event boundaries.
3.1 Models, controller and controls

Three detector seeds are evaluated with one shared generator trained at seed 17. The frozen non-thinking Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 [8] tool controller runs wholly on the RTX 5000 Ada. It starts from STFT evidence and can acquire Fourier/wavelet evidence, verify, or stop within three additional actions. A finite token trie masks generation to legal JSON actions and enumerated reasons for the current candidate and tool budget; the model greedily chooses legal prefixes. The strict parser remains an independent check. Schema validity is enforced by construction, not evidence of acoustic correctness. The LLM cannot overwrite detector probabilities.

The archived unconstrained development run achieved only 50.0% action validity. This engineering failure motivated the decoding amendment before test evaluation; failed traces and source snapshots remain preserved.
Controls include acoustic/foundation baselines, fixed and heuristic verification, the agent without generation, matched V = 0 score controls and component ablations.
3.2 Outcomes and uncertainty

The real primary endpoint is AP against AIS-presence labels. Thresholds are selected on calibration data for a target empirical negative-clip FPR; test recall and FPR are both reported. AP, AUROC and Brier score are computed for every retained record before any referral. Controlled temporal AP uses one-to-one matching at stated IoU thresholds. No primary confidence interval is reported for the single day-vessel component. An optional 2,000-draw paired day-bootstrap interval is nonconfirmatory sensitivity analysis because vessels recur across days. Detector-seed variability is descriptive.
4 Real Detection Results

The agent reached ensemble AP 0.5738, versus 0.5906 for Wavelet, the comparator selected on development data (difference -0.0168). Fixed verification reached 0.5738; its ensemble-AP difference from the agent was +0.000000, with maximum probability difference 1.2e-07. Ensemble AP evaluates averaged per-record probabilities; Table 2 instead averages per-seed AP.
For sensitivity only, the paired day-bootstrap interval is [-0.039, +0.012]. Recurring vessel IDs violate day independence; this interval is nonconfirmatory.

main_paper.caption: Fig. 2. Natural-real detection against AIS labels. Dots/ranges show detector seeds, not independent-record confidence intervals. The operating-point panel uses thresholds fixed on calibration data and shows mean seed-specific rates in percent. Core methods plus the locked comparator are shown; all methods are retained in the exported tables.
main_paper.name: figure2_real_detection

main_paper.text: Table 2. Core comparisons and locked comparator: mean seed-specific metrics. This differs from AP of averaged seed probabilities. All methods are exported.

Mean-seed agent AP was 0.5729; the spectral CNN reached 0.6654. These descriptive test comparisons do not replace the development-locked comparator. At the frozen operating point, agent recall was 1.06% and FPR 0.17%; the low recall limits detection utility.
5 Robustness and Controlled Temporal Detection

Figure 3 tests a separate 120-record metadata-selected subset at seed 17/batch 8, retaining AIS labels under added noise. It covers only numeric fusion, STFT, fixed verification and the agent, not the locked wavelet or all baselines. This is corruption sensitivity, not natural domain shift. The fully synthetic and semi-synthetic temporal studies evaluate a separately trained spectral CNN, not the Qwen/flow method. Their construction labels describe unions of activity; overlapping sources are not resolved instances, and these outcomes cannot establish an agent benefit.

main_paper.caption: Fig. 3. Seed-17 robustness on a separate 120-record metadata-selected subset, not the full 1,200-record three-seed test cohort. Added-noise curves share parents and noise draws; the clean subset is shown separately. The locked wavelet comparator is not part of this four-method study.
main_paper.name: figure3_robustness

main_paper.text: Fixed and agent AP coincided in all 5 conditions. Agent seed-17 AP was 0.6667 on this clean subset and 0.4981 at -5 dB added-noise SNR. These results do not demonstrate an adaptive robustness benefit.

Table 3. Temporal AP means over seeds and declared conditions within each origin/family and IoU: mixed plus fixed SNRs for fully synthetic, three insertion SNRs for semi-synthetic. Origins are not pooled.

Controlled source stems make received interval support observable, but the signals are bounded harmonic, modulated and chirped constructions. A separate semi-synthetic study inserts real AIS-positive excerpts into same-day looped real backgrounds. Its truth is the known insertion union, not audible event truth; source excerpts include their original noise. Origins remain separate; neither supplies human-verified natural event boundaries.
6 Mechanism and Component Ablations

Figure 4 reports the continuous-score controls. Keeping V instead of setting it to zero changed ensemble AP by -0.0257 for fixed verification and -0.0257 for the agent. All three detector-seed differences were negative in each control family. These descriptive contrasts preserve queries, validity and calibration routing.

All 2,205 development clip-seed decisions followed wavelet then fourier then verify. The observed controller therefore behaved as a fixed acquisition sequence; these traces do not establish evidence-dependent adaptation or a reasoning benefit.

All 3,600 held-out test clip-seed decisions acquired all three views and requested verification. Every audited path was wavelet, Fourier, then verify. Verification was the final action, so generated evidence informed no subsequent tool choice. The observed test policy did not perform adaptive tool selection.

The fixed and agent V = 0 controls preserve base logits, acquired views, queries, validity masks, fitting rows and the same two-input positive calibration procedure. Only the entire continuous score V is set to zero. The agent control preserves the original verification-enabled actions, rather than rerunning the no-generation controller. V = 0 removes contrast, dispersion and boundary penalty together, rather than isolating delta alone.

main_paper.caption: Fig. 4. Component AP and matched continuous-score contrasts. Diamonds compare AP of mean-seed probabilities; dots/ranges are paired detector-seed differences, not confidence intervals. Both V = 0 controls retain query, validity and calibration routing. One dependence component precludes an independent-component interval; these are descriptive contributions.
main_paper.name: figure4_mechanism_ablation

main_paper.text: 6.1 Counterfactual interpretation

The intervention is computational. Its sham is constrained to the same support and matched in perturbation energy, but nuisance edits can still change target detectability. The measured paired controls test component utility, not strict physical counterfactual identification. Invalid or unavailable verification returns the base detector output and remains in the denominator.
6.2 HHT numerical failure

HHT reconstruction and a simple-tone check passed, but noisy modes frequently failed extrema or convergence checks. The recorded fractions are 95.8% for the three-second fixture and 100.0% for the ten-second fixture. The exploratory HHT head nevertheless reached mean-seed AP 0.6929. Its descriptive accuracy does not validate the decomposition or promote it into the primary analysis.
7 Compute, Reproducibility and Limitations

main_paper.caption: Fig. 5. Mean detector-seed test AP and actual seed 17 live cost on 32 calibration clips at batch 32, with three warmed passes; horizontal bars show their range, not a confidence interval. Five timed methods include heuristic verification. Model loading is excluded and separately recorded; memory is allocated GPU peak. This measured-method comparison is not an overall cost frontier over unmeasured stronger baselines.
main_paper.name: figure5_accuracy_compute

main_paper.text: The agent cost 346.9 ms/clip, versus 49.4 for fixed verification, 39.0 for the heuristic, 7.1 for numeric fusion and 299.4 without generation. The agent/fixed cost ratio was 7.02; allocated agent peak was 11.37 GiB. These are warm batch-throughput measurements, not single-request latency.

All substantial transforms, fitting and inference use the 32 GB RTX 5000 Ada, selected by UUID. CPU orchestration, I/O, statistical reporting and a small independent spline-reference fixture are incidental. The Thunderbolt connection makes transfer-inclusive measurement essential. Live timings include decoding, transfer, GPU transforms, requested generation, controller calls, classification and frozen calibration. Full primary transform recomputation and unqueried canonical generation companions are charged; no transform-savings claim is made.

Checkpoints preserve model, optimizer, scheduler, random states, configuration fingerprints and the next-batch cursor. Atomic file replacement, fsync, checksum validation and a prior generation support interrupted-run recovery. A separate-process CUDA fixture reproduced the next optimizer step exactly and recovered from a corrupted latest checkpoint copy. This does not protect against storage destruction or establish bitwise reproducibility of every final research kernel.

The strongest limitations are AIS proxies, artificial class balance, one test dependence component, cohort construction, a shared generator seed, a single external GPU/system, and controlled rather than independently annotated real temporal intervals. An agent's rationale is not ground truth. Any gains must be attributed only to contrasts supported by the saved outputs.
8 Conclusion

On this balanced AIS-window cohort, the agent's ensemble AP was below the development-selected Wavelet comparator by a signed difference of -0.0168. Its ensemble AP matched fixed verification while measured cost was 7.02 times higher. The continuous-score contrast against the matched V=0 agent control was -0.0257. All test paths acquired every view and verified last; generated evidence informed no subsequent choice. This execution did not demonstrate improved detection or adaptive tool selection. One connected test component prevents population-level superiority or equivalence inference.

The contribution is the measured failure analysis and matched controls, not a claimed performance gain. Further work requires real event annotations, additional deployments and a demonstrably selective intervention before stronger acoustic or causal claims.

supplement.text: Supplementary Study
Hilbert-Huang and Wavelet Evidence for Underwater Acoustic Detection
S1 Controlled Representation Study

This companion study separates exact construction labels from unknown real-world audibility. Fully synthetic scenes comprise colored ambient noise and zero, one or two harmonic, amplitude-modulated or chirped sources. Received supports include bounded multipath delay. Overlapping source supports are merged into the union of activity for temporal scoring. A union-activity detector does not resolve overlapping physical objects. The separately trained temporal spectral CNN supplies the fully/semi-synthetic results; these do not test Qwen/flow benefit.

The focused representation study uses three-second controlled clips and fixed detection heads for STFT, STFT plus wavelets, STFT plus bounded HHT, and all views. It separates training/development/test generation identities and a held-out signal family. Presence AP in this study is not temporal AP and does not directly establish a reasoning-agent benefit. HHT remains an explicitly exploratory approximation.
Table S1. Recorded controlled representation results, grouped by family and method.

Temporal AP uses greedy confidence-ordered one-to-one matching with the monotone precision envelope. Duplicate predictions count as false positives; classes with no ground-truth events are excluded from mAP and their false positives remain reported. Thresholded event F1 and presence discrimination are additional outcomes, not replacements for a failed temporal endpoint.

No human-verified real temporal intervals were available in this execution. Therefore this supplement makes no claim of real event-boundary accuracy, range/bearing localization, source identity or silent-object detection.
S2 HHT and Wavelet Numerical Validity

The bounded GPU EMD approximation uses up to six modes and ten sifts, piecewise-linear envelopes and masked instantaneous-frequency summaries. It is not relabeled as classical cubic-spline EMD. HHT remains exploratory because the noisy-scene convergence gate failed.

supplement.caption: Fig. S1. Measured numerical fixtures only. The 440 Hz frequency check and small reconstruction errors do not repair the noisy-scene mode failures. The combined flagged-mode fraction includes nonconvergence and extrema failures.
supplement.name: figureS1_hht_numerics

supplement.text: The FFT/Hilbert and wavelet calculations ran on the selected Ada GPU. The small independent spline reference ran on CPU solely as a correctness fixture. Edge effects, mode mixing and low-amplitude instantaneous-frequency instability remain relevant. Exact reconstruction tests summation consistency and cannot establish physically meaningful decomposition.
S3 Controlled Noise Sensitivity and Representation Scope

supplement.caption: Fig. S2. Presence-detection AP for the focused representation study and missing-view tests. Points show available seeds; short horizontal markers are seed means. Missing-view curves retain each family separately. HHT remains exploratory after the numerical convergence failure.
supplement.name: figureS3_representation_study

supplement.text: Table S2. Mean AP by controlled source regime. Regimes are synthetic forms, not vessel classes. Two-source scenes include overlapping and nonoverlapping supports; interval overlap is not required.

Generative replacement can erase all activity in the editable interval. A matched sham may preserve the original waveform additively while still masking it perceptually. Accordingly, detector changes are sensitivity measurements. Generator uncertainty, boundary distortion and invalid replacements must remain visible in the evaluation.
S4 Reproducibility and Resource Accounting
Table S3. Numerical pilot timing. These are single synchronized tensor-resident calls with unequal first-use overhead, not a warmed throughput comparison.

The unconstrained development replay had 50.0% valid actions across 4,220 actions from 2,110 clip-seed records (including partial runs). It failed by proposing already observed STFT after wavelet acquisition. This engineering failure and its traces are preserved. Before test evaluation, the controller was amended to finite legal-JSON token-trie decoding, enforcing schema validity by construction and retaining the independent parser. EOS is required, observed tools are excluded, and no retries choose a favorable action. The 160-state GPU fixture checks integration, not reasoning competence. All 3,600 test clip-seed paths were wavelet, Fourier, then verify; generation informed no later action and did not demonstrate adaptive selection.

Experiment recovery uses project-local atomic checkpoints, checksummed generation metadata, a hash-chained ledger and verified prediction shards. Restarting recomputes unfinished work and preserves completed outputs. Source/configuration/data fingerprints guard against accidental resume under a different experiment.

All code, data, caches, models, figures, reports and restart artifacts remain inside the new MVML2027 submission directory. The earlier submission is unchanged. Large raw data and checkpoints remain outside version control; no publication or submission is performed by generating these drafts.

The main limitations remain five collection days in one dependence component, AIS-derived labels, one port/deployment, 600/600 artificial test balance, a fixed generator seed and construction-only temporal annotation. AP/precision and calibration are not deployment-prevalence estimates. The supplement reports failed numerical assumptions alongside successful fixtures.
